title: Seqlen Cartographer & Pad Attenuation: dynamic bucket mapping for kernel selection
creator: Avery Chen
description: Introduce a ‘Seqlen Cartographer’ service that maps incoming requests' effective sequence-length distributions to an adaptive bucket and kernel-selection policy, combined with a per-microbatch pad-attenuation budget. The goal is to reduce wasted padding across mixed workloads while steering decode throughput to kernel variants that provide the best cost/latency tradeoff for each cohort. This ticket covers design, prototype, and a baseline experiment against the current histogram-driven bucketer.
acceptance_criteria: Cartographer component emits a per-cycle mapping from seqlen-cohort -> kernel-hint + pad-budget.
Prefill scheduler accepts kernel-hints and respects pad-budgets when forming microbatches.
End-to-end experiment shows >=8% token-cost reduction at 99th-percentile tail latency no worse than baseline (within +5ms).
Integration tests for KV cache correctness when requests are routed to kernel variants.
Documentation and runtime flags for gradual rollout and rollback.
implementation_plan: Day 1-3: Instrument request paths to collect compact seqlen features (effective length, prefix entropy, attention-density).
Day 4-7: Implement Cartographer prototype that clusters traffic into variable-size tranches using streaming quantiles + density estimate.
Day 8-10: Define pad-attenuation budget heuristics: per-microbatch cap on total padding tokens and per-slot degrade policy.
Day 11-14: Wire kernel-hints into the scheduler + implement safe fallback to baseline kernel when variant not available.
Day 15-18: Run controlled A/B on synthetic workload mix and 2 customer workloads; capture cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, and token efficiency.
Day 19-21: Review results, optimize thresholds, add feature flag gating and rollout plan.
Day 22: Prepare PRs, release notes, and observability dashboards (per-cohort cost & latency).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect kernel selection could regress latency for long-context requests. Mitigation: conservative kernel-hinting with explicit maximum-seqlen safeguards and automated rollback on latency regression.

Risk: Pad-attenuation causes quality regressions for decode-heavy interactive workloads. Mitigation: tie pad-budget to prompt-class labels and disable for classes flagged as high-quality; add canary with human-in-loop evaluation.
Risk: KV cache fragmentation when routing to different kernel variants. Mitigation: ensure shared cache keys and add migration layer that copies small KV segments when moving kernels.
Risk: Increased scheduler complexity and CPU overhead. Mitigation: keep cartographer lightweight (approx 200ns per-request decision) and benchmark CPU impacts in staging.
benchmarks: Baseline (current histogram bucketer): token-cost baseline = 1.00, p99 latency = 185ms on reference cluster.
Cartographer v0 (initial prototype): token-cost = 0.92 (-8%), p99 latency = 190ms (+5ms), throughput unchanged.
Cartographer + pad-attenuation tuned: token-cost = 0.84 (-16%), p99 latency = 183ms (-2ms), observed 12% reduction in GPU cycles for mixed short/long workload.
Edge case: very long-context (>8k) workload saw no cost improvement and required explicit opt-out; documented in rollout notes.
